label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
Kristen,

Saturday, November 7, about 10:40, I put my popcorn in the break room microwave, hit the popcorn button, and went out front. A customer needed a shear pin for his snowblower, and finding the right one took longer than I expected, maybe six or seven minutes. I left the popcorn unattended. That was my mistake, not anything wrong with the microwave.

The popcorn burned and set off the alarm. We cleared the store for about 25 minutes, and the engine from up on Hertel came. There was no damage, just smoke and a smell that hung around plenty long enough. I’m sorry everybody wound up outside in the cold, and that we lost business over it. The Hendersons usually come back, but that doesn’t excuse sending them home without their cart.

For the record, the September alarm wasn’t mine. That was the sensor in the paint aisle. I’m not trying to dodge Saturday by bringing that up, just keeping the two straight for Gary’s file.

I’ll cover the $175. You can take it from my check or I can bring cash, whichever works better for you.

After 31 years on the job, my first alarm as a civilian was over a bag of butter popcorn. Naturally, Mikey Szymanski was on the engine. I broke him in as a probie in 2003, so I expect to be hearing about this for the rest of my natural life. Fair enough.

I’d really like to keep my Saturday shifts. I like the weekend crowd, and I need the hours for heating oil. I know that means you need to be able to count on me. No more popcorn, and I won’t leave anything cooking unattended again.

Denise’s coffee is on me, too.

Walt
